isolation.concurrencyDecision: 1 validator only for this CLI rerun surface

assertions.title: Limit and skip semantics remain exact under concurrency

steps.action: Run sequential JSONL baseline with `-o jsonl -s 3 -n 7 -t 1 samples/security.evtx`.
steps.observed: Emitted 7 valid JSON records with EventRecordIDs ['4', '5', '6', '7', '8', '9', '10'].

steps.action: Run ordered concurrent JSONL with `-o jsonl -s 3 -n 7 -t 4 samples/security.evtx`.
steps.expected: Emit the same 7 records in the same order as sequential.
steps.observed: Exited 0 but emitted 1 valid JSON record with EventRecordIDs ['10'].

steps.action: Run unordered concurrent JSONL with `-o jsonl -s 3 -n 7 -t 4 --unordered samples/security.evtx`.
steps.expected: Emit the same 7-record set, possibly reordered.
steps.observed: Exited 0 but emitted 1 valid JSON record with EventRecordIDs ['10'].

assertions.issues: Concurrent skip/max selection is still incorrect on the user-facing CLI: both `-t 4` and `-t 4 --unordered` returned only EventRecordID 10 instead of the 7-record subset [4,5,6,7,8,9,10].

assertions.title: Early sink failure stops concurrent output cleanly

steps.action: Run ordered concurrent JSONL through an early-closing pipe consumer.
steps.expected: Process should stop promptly, return the clean exit behavior, and avoid stderr noise.
steps.observed: Captured 2 lines, return code 0, timedOut=False, stderr empty.

steps.action: Run unordered concurrent JSONL through the same early-closing consumer.
steps.expected: Process should stop promptly, return the clean exit behavior, and avoid stderr noise.
steps.observed: Captured 2 lines, return code 0, timedOut=False, stderr empty.

assertions.title: Bugbot concurrency fixes preserve the documented runtime contract

steps.action: Read the current README and architecture excerpts plus the built `--help` output.
steps.expected: Documentation and help should describe ordered output by default, `--unordered` for non-deterministic order, and orchestration-owned cancellation/broken-pipe semantics.
steps.observed: README, docs/architecture.md, and `--help` are aligned on ordered-by-default semantics, `--unordered` behavior, and broken-pipe ownership.
Emitted 100 valid JSON lines with EventRecordIDs 1 through 100.

steps.action: Run concurrent ordered and unordered JSONL commands against the same sample.
steps.expected: Ordered mode should match the sequential output exactly; unordered mode may reorder but must still emit the same logical record set as valid records.
steps.observed: Ordered `-t 4` emitted 9 lines with only 1 valid JSON record and malformed fragments; unordered `-t 4 --unordered` emitted 5 lines with only 1 valid JSON record and malformed fragments.

steps.action: Check the early-closing sink behavior from VAL-BUGBOT-004.
steps.expected: Broken-pipe handling should remain clean at the process boundary.
steps.observed: Broken-pipe handling is now clean, but the ordered/unordered output contract still fails for normal redirected JSONL output.

assertions.issues: The docs/help contract is aligned, but the actual concurrent CLI no longer satisfies it: redirected `-t 4` and `-t 4 --unordered` JSONL output collapsed into one valid record plus malformed fragments instead of preserving the documented ordered/unordered record semantics.

summary: Retested 3 assertions: 1 passed and 2 failed. VAL-BUGBOT-004 now passes with clean broken-pipe exits, while VAL-BUGBOT-003 and VAL-CROSS-002 still fail because concurrent JSONL output under `-t 4` no longer preserves the expected record subset or the documented ordered/unordered output contract.
